podcast.title: Collaborator on Dennis Wilson's "Holy Man"
podcast.body: Roger Taylor contributed to the completion of Dennis Wilson's unfinished song "Holy Man," working alongside Taylor Hawkins and Brian May. This collaboration highlights his respect for and connection with Hawkins. "Taylor added to music, wrote some new lyrics, sang the song, and he was backed up by Roger Taylor and Brian May."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Member of SOS All Stars
podcast.body: Roger Taylor joined Taylor Hawkins and Chad Smith in the one-off drummers' group SOS All Stars for the Live Earth show in London in 2007. This performance brought together influential drummers for a special event. "He was joined by Roger Taylor, of course, and Chad Smith of the Red Hot Chili Peppers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Taylor Hawkins' Favorite Drummer Ever
podcast.body: Roger Taylor was Taylor Hawkins' favorite drummer of all time. This admiration was evident from Hawkins' enthusiastic reaction to a poster of Taylor's solo album "Fun in Space" at the Foo Fighters' studio. "That's Roger Taylor, man. He's my favorite drummer ever."

xref.title: Drowning Accident (1983)
xref.body: Dennis Wilson, a member of The Beach Boys, tragically drowned in a diving accident in 1983. He left behind an unfinished recording titled "Holy Man," which Taylor Hawkins later completed in 2019 with the help of Roger Taylor and Brian May. "Wilson drowned in a diving accident back in 1983."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Initiating "A View to a Kill" Theme (1985)
xref.body: The idea for Duran Duran to create the "A View to a Kill" theme originated with their bass player, Roger Taylor. While reportedly drunk at a party, Taylor approached producer Cubby Broccoli and challenged him about getting "someone decent to do one of your theme songs," an unexpected approach that surprisingly led to the band getting the commission. "Actually it was bass player Roger Taylor who had the idea. He was drunk at a party and he wandered up to producer Cubby Broccoli and said something very close to this. When are you going to get someone decent to do one of your theme songs?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Taylor Hawkins and the Co-Tale Riders (2006)
xref.body: In 2006, Taylor Hawkins formed his own band, Taylor Hawkins and the Co-Tale Riders, a name reflecting his sense of humor and humbleness. The band featured crack session musicians and released three albums, collaborating with figures like Roger Taylor and Brian May (Queen), Nancy Wilson (Heart), Joe Walsh (Eagles), Chrissie Hynde (Pretenders), and LeAnn Rimes. "The first came in 2006 when he formed a band called Taylor Hawkins and the Co-Tale Riders."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: One-Off Drummers Group for Live Earth (2007)
xref.body: SOS All Stars was a unique, one-off group comprised of drummers Taylor Hawkins, Roger Taylor (Queen), and Chad Smith (Red Hot Chili Peppers), assembled specifically for the Live Earth show in London in 2007. This project highlighted a special gathering of influential rock drummers. "This was a one-off drummers group, but together for the live earth show in London in 2007."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: SOS All Stars (2007) - One-Off Drummer Supergroup
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins participated in SOS All Stars, a special one-off drummers' group formed for the Live Earth show in London in 2007. He was joined by Roger Taylor of Queen and Chad Smith of the Red Hot Chili Peppers, showcasing his connections within the drumming community. "In addition to the Coat Tale writers, there was SOS All Stars."

xref.title: Drumming Influences
xref.body: Taylor Hawkins' drumming style was heavily influenced by progressive rock drummers such as Neil Peart of Rush, Stewart Copeland of The Police, and Phil Collins during his time with Genesis. Other influences included Stephen Perkins of Jane's Addiction, Ringo Starr, and his hero, Roger Taylor of Queen. "His heroes were Neil Pirate of Rush, Stuart Copeland of the police, and Phil Collins when he was with Genesis."
